packageRules.description: NODE RUNTIME: the newest stable Node release, not only LTS. .nvmrc holds the major line (26) and is the one source; Docker base images, engines.node, setup-node and any exact pin follow it, all in one 'Node runtime' PR so CI never sees them disagree. Renovate's node versioning counts a new major as unstable until it reaches LTS (about six months after release), so ignoreUnstable is off: a new major is offered as soon as it ships. allowedVersions "<99" is a semver range, which no prerelease (27.0.0-rc.1) satisfies, so alphas and release candidates stay out. rangeStrategy replace keeps a bare major bare (26 -> 27, never 26.14.0) and moves exact pins (26.13.0 -> 26.14.0); the baseline's bump would rewrite .nvmrc and node:26-slim to the full version. A new major still waits for approval on the Dependency Dashboard (the baseline major rule).

engines.node is ">=<major>" and moves with .nvmrc through the custom manager below. The npm manager's own engines dep is off: replace never moves ">=26" (every newer Node satisfies it) and bump rewrites it to ">=26.14.0" on every release.
The package manager version lives in packageManager and is mirrored into the Dockerfile. A bump is a coordinated change, never automerged.
Framework majors reshape the app. Never automerged, and given time to settle.
Test tooling is safe to take quickly; a break shows up immediately and only in CI. Rides in the monthly automerge group.

customManagers.description: engines.node ">=<major>" in any package.json: only the major is captured, so it moves with .nvmrc (">=26" -> ">=27") and a minor or patch release leaves it alone. Its PR joins the Node runtime group above. An engines range in any other shape (">=20.10", "^22") is not matched and is left to the repository.
